evidence_class: Independent mathematical derivation and numerical cross-check; no empirical workbook estimate or biological parameter fit.

model.division: Homogeneous constant per-cell rate lambda; each division replaces parent with two daughters.
model.tag: A forward tag follows one daughter at each division without future information; tag death is final, with no branch replacement.
model.family_selection: A_T={at least one descendant alive at fixed known T}; equal founder weighting or known corrected weights.

definitions.h: P(A_T) in the matched prospective founder population
definitions.T: Known positive observation horizon in arbitrary model time units

model.branching_assumptions: Independent descendant processes; no density dependence, cell types, treatment changes or unmodeled state-dependent rates.

identity.set_relation: {tag alive at T} subset of {family nonextinct at T}

conditional_tag_death_law.interpretation: The law equals a sum of independent Exponential(lambda) and Exponential(mu) waiting times, right-censored at T, for strictly positive rates; zero-rate cases follow by limits. It is symmetric under rate interchange.
conditional_tag_death_law.scope_limit: Unidentifiability statement concerns these conditional tag-death observations alone; it does not cover complete division histories, family-size/tree observations or external rate/selection information.

hidden_conditions_and_limits: The tag must be chosen without knowledge of future outcomes. Following a required terminal survivor or replacing a dead tag changes Q and invalidates exp(-mu*T).
Family inclusion, tag survival, follow-up horizon and exposure must refer to the same target founder population; endpoint-cell size weighting is not equal-founder sampling.
The h denominator must count initially eligible founders, including extinct families, under the matched observation design. A selected table fraction is insufficient.
Observed alive/dead/censored labels and loss to tracking must be known; terminal zeros in an undocumented matrix are not certified survival observations.
For common time-varying death rates, the identity yields exp(-integral_0^T mu(s) ds) and identifies cumulative hazard, not the full time-dependent rate.
For heterogeneous constant founder-specific death rates, the product is a mixture of survivals; -log(Q*h)/T is an effective rate, not proof of a shared individual rate.
Population identity requires T>0 and h>0; finite nonnegative mu implies Q*h>0. A finite-sample zero survival estimate does not prove an infinite biological death rate.
Known h and Q identify mu under this model, not automatically every model parameter or biological mechanism; extra division/tree information may break the rate-swap ambiguity.

Shared-cohort estimates of Q and h have dependence. With complete correctly matched ascertainment, their product equals tag survivors divided by all eligible founders; uncertainty must respect the common denominator.

numerical_cross_check.method: Independent survival ODE h'=(lambda-mu)*h-lambda*h^2, h(0)=1; conditional density from Poisson sibling survival: mu*exp(-mu*t)*(1-exp(-lambda*integral_0^t h(T-s) ds))/h(T). Compared against closed forms, normalization, recovered mu and swapped-rate laws.
numerical_cross_check.implementation_availability: Documented reviewer calculation reproducible from the stated equations, grid and tolerances; no standalone public checker script is supplied.

empirical_application_status: NOT_APPLIED: Oren row selection, original founder denominator, chosen-path rule, observation masks, row joins and timestamps remain unresolved; neither 80/1135 nor 77/1135 is certified h or Q.
novelty: This is a bounded reviewer derivation. Novelty is unestablished; the set identity itself is elementary conditional probability. Prior-art review is separate.
